translation: One must know that warm pathogens shun dispersion; this is not the same method as for sudden exogenous afflictions.
If an external pathogen is contracted first and stirs the lurking heat within, one must first use acrid-cool to resolve the new pathogen, then administer bitter-cold to clear the interior heat.

Moreover, heat is a formless qi, yet the physicians of the time often used digestives to attack the formed, so that the stomach fluids dry up first and the yin fluids are robbed away entirely in many cases.
